newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile approves debt agreements with private banks.
newsitem.headline: Chile approves debt agreements with private banks.

text.p: Chile's chief banking authority gave final approval to debt rescheduling agreements between the central bank and two private institutions, the Banco de Chile and Banco Internacional.
The agreements ease the repayment terms on debts, known as subordinated obligations, which the two private banks incurred during Chile's financial crisis in the early 1980s.

The Banking Superintendency said in a statement it approved the agreements, both signed in July amid controversy over whether the central bank had granted too many concessions in the debt negotiations.
In June, Roberto Zahler resigned as the central bank's president and later charged that its board was granting too many concessions in debt talks.

The Banco de Chile deal allows the institution cancel its $1.7 billion debt with the central bank over 40 years starting in 1997, while Banco Internacional will cancel its debt of $131 million also in 40 annual payments and through placement of new shares. Banco Internacional is not publicly traded.
The superintendency has yet to give final approval to two other subordinated debt deals, involving Banco de Concepcion and Banco Bhif, a superintendency official said.
